fix_description: The date/time token expander that turns replacement placeholders ($YYYY, $MM, $DD, $hh, $mm, $ss) into formatted values fails to substitute $DD (2-digit day-of-month) when it is immediately followed by another uppercase letter, as in '$DDT'. The token-matching logic greedily tries the longer day tokens ($DDDD/$DDD) or mis-computes the token length so the $DD case is skipped, leaving the literal '$DD' in the string; it then survives the Boost regex format pass ($D is not a valid backreference) and appears in the output. Fix the placeholder matcher so $DD is recognized and replaced with the zero-padded day independent of the following character (correct the ordering/length checks of the DDDD/DDD/DD/D alternatives), so 'Scan$YYYY-$MM-$DDT$hh$mm$ss' expands to 'Scan2025-12-10T121915'.
